references.text: God promises to meet Moses at the mercy seat and speak with him there, the same theme of God meeting His people.
God says He will meet Moses at the ark of the testimony, parallel to the promise to meet the people at the entrance of the tabernacle.
Refers to the continual burnt offering (תָּמִיד) that is to be offered throughout all generations.
Detailed description of the daily burnt offering (עֹלַת תָּמִיד) that was to be offered morning and evening.
Confirms that the continual burnt offering was instituted at Mount Sinai.
Daniel prays at the time of the evening offering (עֹלַת), referring to the daily sacrifice.
The prophecy that the continual offering (הַתָּמִיד) will be taken away.
The pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting when the Lord spoke with Moses.
The tent of meeting (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) as the place where God meets His people.
Contrasts the continual offering in the Old Testament with Christ's perfect sacrifice once for all.
Both verses establish 'continual' (everlasting) ritual acts before the Lord's face as a symbol of God's unbroken presence.
Illustrates the ritual necessity to meet God at the entrance: cleansing by blood at the altar.
Highlights the necessary purification as a prerequisite for meeting God at the altar in the tent of meeting.
Confirms that the purpose of the burnt offering at the entrance is to create favor and encounter before the Lord's face.
Specifies the process for meeting God at the entrance through the presentation and slaughter of the sacrificial animal.
